claims.evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 2B).

claims.claim: SLAH3-FLAG does not associate with BIK1-T7 in N. benthamiana.
claims.source: To independently confirm the PBL27-SLAH3 interaction in N. benthamiana, we immuno-precipitated SLAH3-FLAG and observed that it associated with PBL27-T7 but not BIK1-T7, and that the association was independent of chitin stimulation (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 2B).

claims.claim: The association between SLAH3 and PBL27 is independent of chitin stimulation.
claims.source: To independently confirm the PBL27-SLAH3 interaction in N. benthamiana, we immuno-precipitated SLAH3-FLAG and observed that it associated with PBL27-T7 but not BIK1-T7, and that the association was independent of chitin stimulation (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments with and without chitin treatment (Figure 2B).

claims.claim: SLAH3 exists in a complex with PBL27 in a chitin-independent manner.
claims.source: Together, these results show that SLAH3 exists in a complex with PBL27 in a chitin-independent manner.
claims.evidence: Supported by BiFC and co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 2A, 2B).

claims.claim: PBL27 trans-phosphorylates SLAH3-N in vitro.
claims.source: In vitro phosphorylation experiments using N- and C-terminal domains of SLAH3 indicated that PBL27, but not its kinase dead variant PBL27K112E, trans-phosphorylated both the N-and C-terminal domain of SLAH3 (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays (Figure 2C).

claims.claim: PBL27 trans-phosphorylates SLAH3-C in vitro.
claims.source: In vitro phosphorylation experiments using N- and C-terminal domains of SLAH3 indicated that PBL27, but not its kinase dead variant PBL27K112E, trans-phosphorylated both the N-and C-terminal domain of SLAH3 (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays (Figure 2C).

claims.claim: PBL27 kinase dead variant does not trans-phosphorylate SLAH3-N or SLAH3-C in vitro.
claims.source: In vitro phosphorylation experiments using N- and C-terminal domains of SLAH3 indicated that PBL27, but not its kinase dead variant PBL27K112E, trans-phosphorylated both the N-and C-terminal domain of SLAH3 (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays (Figure 2C).

claims.claim: A weaker in vitro trans-phosphorylation was observed for SLAH3-C compared with SLAH3-N.
claims.source: Of note, a weaker in vitro trans-phosphorylation could be observed for SLAH3-C compared with SLAH3-N (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays (Figure 2C).

claims.claim: PBL27 directly interacts with SLAH3.
claims.source: The finding that PBL27 phosphorylates SLAH3 in vitro also provides evidence for a direct interaction between these two proteins, which is consistent with our BiFC and co-immunoprecipitation results (Figure 2A and B).
claims.evidence: Inferred from in vitro phosphorylation experiments and supported by BiFC and co-immunoprecipitation results (Figure 2A, 2B, 2C).

claims.claim: SLAH3-N and SLAH3-C are phosphorylated more strongly when incubated with PBL27-HA purified from chitin-treated plants.
claims.source: Both SLAH3-N and SLAH3-C were clearly phosphorylated when incubated with PBL27-HA, which was significantly stronger when PBL27-HA was purified from chitin-treated plants (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays using PBL27-HA from chitin-treated and untreated plants (Figure 2D).

claims.claim: PBL27 is able to trans-phosphorylate SLAH3-N and SLAH3-C depending on chitin stimulation.
claims.source: This revealed that PBL27 is able to trans-phosphorylate SLAH3-N and SLAH3-C depending on chitin stimulation.
claims.evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays using PBL27-HA from chitin-treated and untreated plants (Figure 2D).

claims.claim: Elicitation with chitin led to SLAH3 phosphorylation in vivo.
claims.source: Elicitation with chitin led to SLAH3 phosphorylation, as indicated by a band shift, which can be reversed upon phosphatase treatment (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: Supported by Phos-tag SDS-PAGE analysis (Figure 2E).

claims.claim: SLAH3 phosphorylation status can be regulated by PBL27 and depends on chitin stimulation.
claims.source: Together, our in vitro and in vivo data provide evidence that SLAH3 phosphorylation status can be regulated by PBL27 and depends on chitin stimulation.
claims.evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assays and Phos-tag SDS-PAGE analysis (Figure 2D, 2E).

claims.claim: SLAH3 remained silent when injected into Xenopus oocytes alone.
claims.source: In two-electrode voltage clamp (TEVC) experiments SLAH3 remained silent when it was injected into Xenopus oocytes alone (Figure 3A) (Geiger et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by TEVC experiments (Figure 3A) and citation to Geiger et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Co-injection of SLAH3 with PBL27 generated macroscopic S-type anion currents.
claims.source: By contrast, co-injection with PBL27 generated macroscopic S-type anion currents (Figure 3A), with current amplitudes of 8 µA similar to SLAH3 activated by calcium-insensitive CPK21ΔEF or CBL1/CIPK23 (Figure 3B) (Maierhofer et al., 2014a; Geiger et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by TEVC experiments (Figure 3A, 3B).

claims.claim: PBL27 is sufficient to trigger SLAH3-mediated anion transport independent of ABA signalling.
claims.source: This suggests that PBL27 is sufficient to trigger SLAH3-mediated anion transport independent of ABA signalling (Geiger et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Inferred from ABI1 co-injection experiments and supported by citation to Geiger et al., 2010.

claims.claim: PBL27 did not activate SLAC1.
claims.source: Here it should be noted that PBL27 did not activate SLAC1, unlike OST1 and CBL1/CIPK23 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and which is consistent with wild type-like stomatal closure in slac1 mutants (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).

claims.claim: OST1 activates SLAC1.
claims.source: Here it should be noted that PBL27 did not activate SLAC1, unlike OST1 and CBL1/CIPK23 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and which is consistent with wild type-like stomatal closure in slac1 mutants (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).

claims.claim: CBL1/CIPK23 activates SLAC1.
claims.source: Here it should be noted that PBL27 did not activate SLAC1, unlike OST1 and CBL1/CIPK23 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and which is consistent with wild type-like stomatal closure in slac1 mutants (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).

claims.claim: SLAH3-mediated anion current amplitudes were strongly increased in the presence of CERK1 co-injection when activated by PBL27.
claims.source: SLAH3-mediated anion current amplitudes were strongly increased in the presence of CERK1 but not LYK5 co-injection, when activated by PBL27 (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3C).

claims.claim: SLAH3-mediated anion current amplitudes were not increased in the presence of LYK5 co-injection when activated by PBL27.
claims.source: SLAH3-mediated anion current amplitudes were strongly increased in the presence of CERK1 but not LYK5 co-injection, when activated by PBL27 (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3C).

claims.claim: When LYK5 and CERK1 were co-injected without PBL27, SLAH3 remained silent.
claims.source: When LYK5 and CERK1 were co-injected without PBL27, SLAH3 remained silent (Figure 3C), corresponding with SLAH3 interaction with PBL27 but not CERK1 (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3C).

claims.claim: Only signalling-competent CERK1 amplified PBL27-mediated SLAH3 activation.
claims.source: Consistent with the finding that PBL27 is phosphorylated by CERK1 (Shinya et al., 2014), only signalling-competent CERK1 amplified PBL27-mediated SLAH3 activation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D) and citation to Shinya et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Activation of SLAH3 by PBL27 was dependent on its kinase activity.
claims.source: Activation of SLAH3 by PBL27 was dependent on its kinase activity (Figure 3B), which was also necessary for amplified SLAH3 activation by CERK1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments using kinase dead PBL27 (Figure 3B).

claims.claim: PBL27 kinase activity was necessary for amplified SLAH3 activation by CERK1.
claims.source: Activation of SLAH3 by PBL27 was dependent on its kinase activity (Figure 3B), which was also necessary for amplified SLAH3 activation by CERK1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).

claims.claim: The phosphorylation status of PBL27 correlates with the activation of SLAH3.
claims.source: This suggests that the phosphorylation status of PBL27 correlates with the activation of SLAH3 and is in agreement with enhanced phosphorylation of SLAH3 when PBL27 was purified from chitin-stimulated cells (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: Inferred from oocyte experiments and supported by in vitro kinase assays (Figure 2D, Figure 3).

claims.claim: Co-injection with CERK1 inhibited PBL1 activation of SLAH3.
claims.source: Unexpectedly, co-injection with CERK1 inhibited PBL1 activation of SLAH3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).

claims.claim: PBL27 is the primary kinase that directly phosphorylates SLAH3 for the release of anions.
claims.source: We conclude that PBL27 is the primary kinase that directly phosphorylates SLAH3 for the release of anions and functions in an activation status-dependent manner regulated by CERK1.
claims.evidence: Inferred from multiple experiments showing PBL27 phosphorylates and activates SLAH3, and CERK1 amplifies this activation.

claims.claim: PBL27 functions in an activation status-dependent manner regulated by CERK1.
claims.source: We conclude that PBL27 is the primary kinase that directly phosphorylates SLAH3 for the release of anions and functions in an activation status-dependent manner regulated by CERK1.
claims.evidence: Inferred from experiments showing CERK1 amplifies PBL27-mediated SLAH3 activation.

claims.claim: SLAH3 was phosphorylated at S127, S189, and S601 by PBL27 in vitro.
claims.source: We discovered that SLAH3 was phosphorylated at three sites by PBL27: S127 and S189 at SLAH3-N and S601 at SLAH3-C (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B and C).
claims.evidence: Supported by LC-MS/MS analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B and C).

claims.claim: Single phospho-mimic mutations of S127, S189 and S601 did not auto-activate SLAH3.
claims.source: In oocytes, injection of single phospho-mimic mutations of S127, S189 and S601 (S127D, S189D and S601D) did not auto-activate SLAH3 and had no impact on PBL27 activation of SLAH3 (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3D).

claims.claim: The double mutant S127D/S189D was constitutive active.
claims.source: However, remarkably, the double mutant S127D/S189D, but neither S127D/S601D nor S189D/S601D, was constitutive active (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3E).

claims.claim: S127D/S601D was not constitutive active.
claims.source: However, remarkably, the double mutant S127D/S189D, but neither S127D/S601D nor S189D/S601D, was constitutive active (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3E).

claims.claim: S189D/S601D was not constitutive active.
claims.source: However, remarkably, the double mutant S127D/S189D, but neither S127D/S601D nor S189D/S601D, was constitutive active (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3E).

claims.claim: Co-expression of S127D/S189D with PBL27 did not result in a further increase in anion currents.
claims.source: Interestingly, co-expression of S127D/S189D with PBL27 did not result in a further increase in anion currents whereas S127D/S601D and S189D/S601D could still be activated by PBL27 (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3E).

claims.claim: S127D/S601D and S189D/S601D could still be activated by PBL27.
claims.source: Interestingly, co-expression of S127D/S189D with PBL27 did not result in a further increase in anion currents whereas S127D/S601D and S189D/S601D could still be activated by PBL27 (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3E).

claims.claim: The phosphorylation status of both S127 and S189 is critical for SLAH3 channel opening.
claims.source: These results provide evidence that the phosphorylation status of both S127 and S189 is critical for SLAH3 channel opening.
claims.evidence: Inferred from oocyte experiments showing S127D/S189D double mutant is constitutive active (Figure 3E).

claims.claim: PBL27 activation of SLAH3 is abrogated by S127A.
claims.source: Importantly, we observed that PBL27 activation of SLAH3 is abrogated by S127A, but not S189 and S601 (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3F).

claims.claim: PBL27 activation of SLAH3 is not abrogated by S189A.
claims.source: Importantly, we observed that PBL27 activation of SLAH3 is abrogated by S127A, but not S189 and S601 (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3F).

claims.claim: PBL27 activation of SLAH3 is not abrogated by S601A.
claims.source: Importantly, we observed that PBL27 activation of SLAH3 is abrogated by S127A, but not S189 and S601 (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3F).

claims.claim: S127A did not affect the activation of SLAH3 by CPK21ΔEF and CBL1/CIPK23.
claims.source: We also found that S127A did not affect the activation of SLAH3 by other kinases such as CPK21ΔEF and CBL1/CIPK23 or by the heteromerization with the silent anion channel subunit SLAH1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) (Cubero-Font et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).

claims.claim: S127A did not affect the activation of SLAH3 by heteromerization with SLAH1.
claims.source: We also found that S127A did not affect the activation of SLAH3 by other kinases such as CPK21ΔEF and CBL1/CIPK23 or by the heteromerization with the silent anion channel subunit SLAH1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) (Cubero-Font et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) and citation to Cubero-Font et al., 2016.

claims.claim: PBL27 regulates SLAH3 activation through phosphorylation of S127, a site not required for CPK21 and CBL1/CIPK23 activation of SLAH3.
claims.source: These results demonstrate that PBL27 regulates SLAH3 activation through phosphorylation of S127, a site not required for CPK21 and CBL1/CIPK23 activation of SLAH3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).

claims.claim: S127 phosphorylation is required for SLAH3 activation by PBL27 but not sufficient by itself to induce anion transport.
claims.source: However, whilst S127 phosphorylation is required for SLAH3 activation by PBL27, it is not sufficient by itself to induce anion transport (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments showing S127D alone does not auto-activate SLAH3 (Figure 3D).

claims.claim: S127 can only auto-activate SLAH3 in the context of additional S189 phospho-mimicry.
claims.source: It can only auto-activate SLAH3 in the context of additional S189 phospho-mimicry (Figure 3E), and thus suggests a functional link between these two residues in SLAH3 channel opening.
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments showing S127D/S189D double mutant is constitutive active (Figure 3E).

claims.claim: The S189A mutation resulted in constitutive activation of SLAH3.
claims.source: Surprisingly, the S189A instead of the S189D mutation resulted in constitutive activation of SLAH3 (Figure 3D and F).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3D, 3F).

claims.claim: The S189A auto-activation could not be further elevated by co-injection of PBL27, CIPK23/CBL1, or SLAH1.
claims.source: The S189A auto-activation could not be further elevated by co-injection of PBL27 or other anion channel activating components like CIPK23/CBL1 or SLAH1 (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).

claims.claim: CERK1-mediated amplification of SLAH3 activation by PBL27 is compromised in the S189A constitutive active variant of SLAH3.
claims.source: However, CERK1-mediated amplification of SLAH3 activation by PBL27 is compromised in the S189A constitutive active variant of SLAH3 (Figure 3G).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3G).

claims.claim: PBL27 phosphorylation of S127 activates SLAH3 but full opening of the SLAH3 channel additionally requires PBL27 phosphorylation of S189, in a CERK1-dependent manner.
claims.source: Thus, it seems that PBL27 phosphorylation of S127 activates SLAH3 but full opening of the SLAH3 channel additionally requires PBL27 phosphorylation of S189, in a CERK1-dependent manner.
claims.evidence: Inferred from oocyte experiments showing S127A abrogates PBL27 activation and S189A compromises CERK1-dependent amplification (Figure 3F, 3G).

claims.claim: S601 is not involved in phosphorylation-dependent or -independent activation of SLAH3.
claims.source: S601 seems not to be involved in phosphorylation-dependent or -independent activation of SLAH3, since the mutant S601A could be either activated by PBL27 (Figure 3F) or by CPK21ΔEF, CIPK23/CBL1 and SLAH1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
claims.evidence: Supported by oocyte experiments (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).

claims.claim: Transgenic slah3 plants expressing wild-type SLAH3 showed chitin-induced stomatal closure.
claims.source: Transgenic slah3 plants expressing wild-type SLAH3 showed chitin-induced stomatal closure (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: Supported by stomatal aperture measurements (Figure 4A).

claims.claim: Plants expressing the S127A variant failed to close stomata in response to chitin.
claims.source: By contrast, plants expressing the S127A and S189A variants failed to close stomata in response to chitin, similar to slah3 mutants (Figure 4B and C).
claims.evidence: Supported by stomatal aperture measurements (Figure 4B).

claims.claim: Plants expressing the S189A variant failed to close stomata in response to chitin.
claims.source: By contrast, plants expressing the S127A and S189A variants failed to close stomata in response to chitin, similar to slah3 mutants (Figure 4B and C).
claims.evidence: Supported by stomatal aperture measurements (Figure 4C).

claims.claim: Plants expressing the S601A SLAH3 variant behaved wild type-like in chitin-induced stomatal closure.
claims.source: As expected from oocyte experiments (Figure 3F), plants expressing the S601A SLAH3 variant behaved wild type-like (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: Supported by stomatal aperture measurements (Figure 4D).

claims.claim: Mutant slah3 plants developed larger disease lesions from B. cinerea three days post inoculation relative to Col-0.
claims.source: Lesion diameter analysis revealed that relative to Col-0 and complementation lines expressing SLAH3 wild type, mutant slah3 plants and complementation lines expressing S127A and S189A, but not S601A, developed larger disease lesions three days post inoculation (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Supported by lesion diameter measurements (Figure 5A).

claims.claim: Complementation lines expressing S127A developed larger disease lesions from B. cinerea three days post inoculation relative to Col-0.
claims.source: Lesion diameter analysis revealed that relative to Col-0 and complementation lines expressing SLAH3 wild type, mutant slah3 plants and complementation lines expressing S127A and S189A, but not S601A, developed larger disease lesions three days post inoculation (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Supported by lesion diameter measurements (Figure 5A).

claims.claim: Complementation lines expressing S189A developed larger disease lesions from B. cinerea three days post inoculation relative to Col-0.
claims.source: Lesion diameter analysis revealed that relative to Col-0 and complementation lines expressing SLAH3 wild type, mutant slah3 plants and complementation lines expressing S127A and S189A, but not S601A, developed larger disease lesions three days post inoculation (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Supported by lesion diameter measurements (Figure 5A).

claims.claim: Complementation lines expressing S601A did not develop larger disease lesions from B. cinerea three days post inoculation relative to Col-0.
claims.source: Lesion diameter analysis revealed that relative to Col-0 and complementation lines expressing SLAH3 wild type, mutant slah3 plants and complementation lines expressing S127A and S189A, but not S601A, developed larger disease lesions three days post inoculation (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Supported by lesion diameter measurements (Figure 5A).

claims.claim: slah3 mutants showed wild type-like chitin-induced ROS burst.
claims.source: Notably, slah3 mutants were not generally immune-compromised, since we observed wild type-like chitin-induced ROS burst and ethylene production (Figure 5B and C).
claims.evidence: Supported by ROS production measurements (Figure 5B).

claims.claim: slah3 mutants showed wild type-like chitin-induced ethylene production.
claims.source: Notably, slah3 mutants were not generally immune-compromised, since we observed wild type-like chitin-induced ROS burst and ethylene production (Figure 5B and C).
claims.evidence: Supported by ethylene accumulation measurements (Figure 5C).

claims.claim: The chitin-induced ROS burst was not altered in pbl27 mutants.
claims.source: We also found that the chitin-induced ROS burst was not altered in pbl27 mutants (Figure 5D), consistent with previous studies (Shinya et al., 2014) and that PBL27 showed no interaction with RBOHD (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: Supported by ROS production measurements (Figure 5D) and citation to Shinya et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Examination of B. cinerea infection in pbl27 revealed no significant differences compared with wild type.
claims.source: Examination of B. cinerea infection in pbl27 revealed no significant differences compared with wild type (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: Supported by lesion diameter measurements (Figure 5E).

claims.claim: S127 and S189 are important for SLAH3 function in resistance to B. cinerea.
claims.source: Our infection studies revealed that S127 and S189 are important for SLAH3 function in resistance to B. cinerea.
claims.evidence: Supported by lesion diameter measurements showing S127A and S189A lines developed larger lesions (Figure 5A).

claims.claim: The same phospho-sites regulate chitin-induced stomatal closure and anti-fungal immunity at the whole leaf level.
claims.source: Thus, the same phospho-sites regulate chitin-induced stomatal closure and anti-fungal immunity at the whole leaf level.
claims.evidence: Inferred from stomatal closure and infection assays showing S127 and S189 are required for both processes (Figure 4, Figure 5A).

claims.claim: Many agronomical important pathogens penetrate plant tissues directly through the epidermis or via stomata.
claims.source: Many agronomical important pathogens penetrate plant tissues directly through the epidermis or via stomata (Grimmer et al., 2012; Faulkner and Robatzek, 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Grimmer et al., 2012 and Faulkner and Robatzek, 2012.

claims.claim: Fungal pathogens are the causal agents of devastating diseases such as rust fungi.
claims.source: These include fungal pathogens that are the causal agents of devastating diseases such as rust fungi (Fones et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2016; Bebber and Gurr, 2015; Shafiei et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Fones et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2016; Bebber and Gurr, 2015; Shafiei et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Epidermal cells are highly immunomodulatory to oligosaccharides of fungal chitin.
claims.source: To defend fungal infection at the level of penetration, epidermal cells are highly immunomodulatory to oligosaccharides of fungal chitin, a microbe-associated molecular pattern (MAMP) present across fungal families (Faulkner and Robatzek, 2012; McLachlan et al., 2014; Koers et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Faulkner and Robatzek, 2012; McLachlan et al., 2014; Koers et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Chitin is a microbe-associated molecular pattern (MAMP) present across fungal families.

claims.evidence: Supported by citations and established knowledge.

claims.claim: In Arabidopsis, perception of chitin is mediated at the cell surface by three related pattern recognition receptors (PRRs).
claims.source: In Arabidopsis, perception of chitin is mediated at the cell surface by three related pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) (Boutrot and Zipfel, 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Boutrot and Zipfel, 2017.

claims.claim: CERK1 and LYK5 encode single-pass transmembrane receptor kinases.
claims.source: CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE 1 (CERK1) and LYSINE MOTIF (LysM) RECEPTOR KINASE 5 (LYK5) encode single-pass transmembrane receptor kinases (Liu et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2012.

claims.claim: LYM2 encodes a receptor-like protein predominantly present at plasmodesmal membranes and specifically involved in cell-to-cell signalling.
claims.source: LysM-domain-containing GLYCOSYLPHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL (GPI)-anchored protein 2 (LYM2) encodes a receptor-like protein predominantly present at plasmodesmal membranes and specifically involved in cell-to-cell signalling (Faulkner et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Faulkner et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The middle LysM domain of CERK1 was shown to bind directly to chitin oligomers.
claims.source: Their ectodomains consist of three LysM domains, of which in CERK1 the middle LysM domain was shown to bind directly to chitin oligomers (Liu et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2012.

claims.claim: LYK5 is the major chitin receptor in Arabidopsis, binding chitin oligomers with higher affinity than CERK1.
claims.source: Recent data demonstrate that LYK5 is the major chitin receptor in Arabidopsis, binding chitin oligomers with higher affinity than CERK1 (Cao et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Cao et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Upon chitin binding, LYK5 forms a complex with CERK1 leading to signal generation.
claims.source: Upon chitin binding, LYK5 forms a complex with CERK1 leading to signal generation, which depends on CERK1 autophosphorylation at specific threonine and tyrosine residues and dephosphorylation by the CERK1-INTERACTING PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE 1 (CIPP1) phosphatase (Cao et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Suzuki et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Suzuki et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Signal generation from LYK5-CERK1 complex depends on CERK1 autophosphorylation at specific threonine and tyrosine residues.
claims.source: Upon chitin binding, LYK5 forms a complex with CERK1 leading to signal generation, which depends on CERK1 autophosphorylation at specific threonine and tyrosine residues and dephosphorylation by the CERK1-INTERACTING PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE 1 (CIPP1) phosphatase (Cao et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Suzuki et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Suzuki et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Signal generation from LYK5-CERK1 complex depends on dephosphorylation by CIPP1 phosphatase.
claims.source: Upon chitin binding, LYK5 forms a complex with CERK1 leading to signal generation, which depends on CERK1 autophosphorylation at specific threonine and tyrosine residues and dephosphorylation by the CERK1-INTERACTING PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE 1 (CIPP1) phosphatase (Cao et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Suzuki et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Suzuki et al., 2016.

claims.claim: A key event of PRR signalling is the phosphorylation of receptor complex-associated RECEPTOR-LIKE CYTOPLASMIC KINASES (RLCKs).

results.result: LYK5, CERK1, PBL27, and SLAH3 are required for chitin-induced stomatal closure in Arabidopsis. Mutants of cerk1, lyk5, pbl27, and slah3 fail to close stomata in response to chitin treatment, while lyk2, lyk3, lyk4, and slac1 mutants behave like wild-type. Complementation with GFP-tagged variants restores chitin-induced stomatal closure.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C10-C12, C15-C20 provide converging genetic evidence from multiple independent mutants and complementation lines showing that LYK5, CERK1, PBL27, and SLAH3 are specifically required for chitin-induced stomatal closure (Figure 1A-C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1). The complementation experiments validate that the phenotypes are due to loss of the specific genes. Statistical analysis shows significant differences (p<0.05) between control and chitin treatments.

results.result: PBL27 directly interacts with SLAH3 in a chitin-independent manner. BiFC experiments show fluorescent signals between SLAH3-YFPn and PBL27-YFPc but not between SLAH3 and CERK1 kinase-dead or BIK1. Co-immunoprecipitation confirms the SLAH3-PBL27 association is independent of chitin stimulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C23-C24, C26, C32-C35, C40 provide multiple lines of evidence for direct SLAH3-PBL27 interaction using complementary approaches (BiFC in Figure 2A, co-IP in Figure 2B). The chitin-independence is demonstrated by co-IP experiments with and without chitin treatment. The specificity is shown by lack of interaction with BIK1 and CERK1 kinase-dead variant.

results.result: PBL27 phosphorylates SLAH3 at S127, S189, and S601 in vitro, with enhanced phosphorylation when PBL27 is purified from chitin-treated plants. In vivo, chitin treatment induces SLAH3 phosphorylation as detected by Phos-tag SDS-PAGE.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C36-C39, C41-C44, C63 provide robust biochemical evidence for PBL27-mediated SLAH3 phosphorylation using in vitro kinase assays (Figure 2C-D), LC-MS/MS identification of phosphorylation sites (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and in vivo phosphorylation detection (Figure 2E). The kinase-dead PBL27 variant serves as an appropriate negative control. The chitin-dependent enhancement is quantitatively demonstrated.

results.result: PBL27 activates SLAH3-mediated S-type anion currents in Xenopus oocytes independent of ABA signaling. SLAH3 remains silent when injected alone but generates macroscopic anion currents (~8 µA) when co-injected with PBL27. PBL27 does not activate SLAC1, and activation requires PBL27 kinase activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C46, C49-C52, C57 demonstrate PBL27-specific activation of SLAH3 using two-electrode voltage clamp experiments in oocytes (Figure 3A-B). The ABA-independence is shown by lack of ABI1 suppression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A). The specificity for SLAH3 over SLAC1 and requirement for kinase activity are demonstrated with appropriate controls including kinase-dead PBL27.

results.result: CERK1 amplifies PBL27-mediated SLAH3 activation in a signaling-dependent manner. Co-injection of CERK1 with PBL27 strongly increases SLAH3-mediated anion currents, while LYK5 co-injection has no effect. Only signaling-competent CERK1 amplifies activation, and PBL27 kinase activity is required for this amplification.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C53-C56, C58, C61-C62 demonstrate CERK1-dependent amplification of SLAH3 activation using oocyte electrophysiology (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2). The requirement for signaling-competent CERK1 and active PBL27 kinase is shown with appropriate mutant controls. The data support a model where CERK1 phosphorylates and activates PBL27, which then phosphorylates SLAH3.

results.result: S127 and S189 are critical phosphorylation sites for SLAH3 activation by PBL27. The S127A mutation abrogates PBL27 activation, while the double phospho-mimic S127D/S189D is constitutively active. Single phospho-mimic mutations do not auto-activate SLAH3, demonstrating that both sites are required for channel opening.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C73, C76-C78 provide systematic mutagenesis analysis of SLAH3 phosphorylation sites using oocyte electrophysiology (Figure 3D-F). The data show that S127 is specifically required for PBL27 activation (not for other kinases), and both S127 and S189 phosphorylation are needed for channel opening. The constitutive activity of S127D/S189D double mutant provides strong evidence for the functional importance of both sites.

results.result: S189 has a dual role in SLAH3 function: the S189A mutation causes constitutive activation that cannot be further elevated by PBL27 or other activators, but compromises CERK1-dependent amplification of SLAH3 activation. This suggests S189 is required for full CERK1-dependent channel opening.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C82, C144 reveal an unexpected property of S189 using oocyte experiments (Figure 3D, F-G). The constitutive activity of S189A is well-documented, but its inability to be further activated and its compromised CERK1-dependent amplification suggest a complex regulatory role. However, the mechanistic interpretation of why S189A is constitutively active remains unclear and may require additional structural or biochemical studies.

results.result: S601 is not involved in phosphorylation-dependent or -independent activation of SLAH3. The S601A mutant can be activated by PBL27, CPK21ΔEF, CIPK23/CBL1, and SLAH1 similar to wild-type SLAH3.
results.evaluation: Claim C83 is supported by oocyte experiments showing S601A behaves like wild-type SLAH3 with multiple activators (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3C). This negative result is important for defining which phosphorylation sites are functionally relevant for SLAH3 activation.

results.result: S127 and S189 residues of SLAH3 are required for chitin-induced stomatal closure in planta. Transgenic slah3 plants expressing wild-type SLAH3 show chitin-induced closure, while plants expressing S127A or S189A variants fail to close stomata in response to chitin. The S601A variant behaves like wild-type.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C84-C87 validate the functional importance of S127 and S189 in the physiological context using complementation experiments in Arabidopsis (Figure 4A-D). The data are consistent with the oocyte experiments and demonstrate that these phosphorylation sites are required for chitin-induced stomatal closure in intact plants. Statistical analysis shows significant differences (p<0.05) between genotypes.

results.result: S127 and S189 residues of SLAH3 are required for anti-fungal immunity at the whole leaf level. slah3 mutants and complementation lines expressing S127A or S189A develop larger disease lesions from B. cinerea infection compared to wild-type, while S601A lines behave like wild-type.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C88-C91, C96-C97 demonstrate that the same phosphorylation sites required for stomatal closure are also important for resistance to fungal infection (Figure 5A). The lesion diameter measurements show statistically significant differences (p<0.05) between genotypes. This connects the molecular mechanism to a physiologically relevant immune response, though the manuscript acknowledges that direct causality between stomatal closure and whole-leaf immunity remains to be tested.

results.result: slah3 and pbl27 mutants are not generally immune-compromised. slah3 mutants show wild-type chitin-induced ROS burst and ethylene production, and pbl27 mutants show wild-type chitin-induced ROS burst and no significant difference in B. cinerea infection compared to wild-type.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C95 provide important controls showing that the immune defects in slah3 mutants are specific to SLAH3-dependent processes and not due to general immune deficiency (Figure 5B-E). The ROS and ethylene measurements demonstrate that other immune responses remain intact. The lack of B. cinerea susceptibility in pbl27 mutants is explained by potential redundancy with PBL1.

results.result: The LYK5-CERK1-PBL27-SLAH3 pathway represents a short signal transduction module from MAMP recognition to anion channel activation, independent of ABA signaling. PBL27 pre-exists in a complex with SLAH3, and upon chitin stimulation, activated PBL27 phosphorylates SLAH3 to trigger anion release and stomatal closure.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C140-C143, C145, C148-C150, C155 synthesize the major findings into a coherent model supported by genetic, biochemical, and electrophysiological data. The independence from ABA signaling is demonstrated by ABI1 experiments. The pre-existing complex and chitin-dependent activation are shown by co-IP and phosphorylation assays. The model is well-supported by the collective evidence, though some mechanistic details (e.g., how CERK1 amplifies SLAH3 opening) remain to be fully elucidated.

results.result: Prior work establishes that LYK5 is the major chitin receptor forming a complex with CERK1, PBL27 is phosphorylated by CERK1 signaling, CERK1 binds chitin and chitosan, BIK1 associates with CERK1 and activates RBOHD-mediated ROS burst to flagellin, and pbl27 mutants are not compromised in chitin-induced ROS.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C14, C22, C25, C27-C31 accurately cite and represent prior published work (Cao et al., 2014; Shinya et al., 2014; Petutschnig et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2010; Kadota et al., 2014; Li et al., 2014). The BiFC experiments in this manuscript (Figure 2A) confirm some of these interactions (CERK1-LYK5, BIK1-RBOHD). These claims provide appropriate context for the current work.

results.result: Stomata of slah3 mutants show intermediate levels of closure to chitosan, not significantly different from chitosan-stimulated wild-type guard cells or unstimulated slah3 guard cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C21 describes an intermediate phenotype for chitosan response in slah3 mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 2). However, the statistical analysis indicates the intermediate value is not significantly different from either wild-type chitosan-treated or slah3 untreated controls, making the interpretation ambiguous. The authors suggest this could indicate redundancy with SLAC1 for chitosan responses, but this requires further investigation.

results.result: Co-injection with CERK1 inhibits PBL1 activation of SLAH3 in oocytes.
results.evaluation: Claim C60 reports an unexpected inhibitory effect of CERK1 on PBL1-mediated SLAH3 activation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E). While the observation is supported by the data, the mechanism is unclear. The authors speculate this may relate to PBL1 functioning downstream of different PRRs (PEPR1/2), but this requires further investigation.

results.result: The S127A mutation does not affect SLAH3 activation by CPK21ΔEF, CBL1/CIPK23, or heteromerization with SLAH1, demonstrating that S127 is specifically required for PBL27-mediated activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C75 demonstrate the specificity of S127 for PBL27-mediated activation using oocyte experiments with multiple alternative activators (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A). This is important for showing that S127 is not a general activation site but is specific to the PBL27 pathway.

results.result: The phosphorylation status of PBL27 correlates with the activation of SLAH3.
results.evaluation: Claim C59 is inferred from multiple experiments showing that CERK1-phosphorylated PBL27 more strongly activates SLAH3 (Figure 3, Figure 2D). The correlation is well-supported, though direct measurement of PBL27 phosphorylation status in the oocyte experiments would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: Background and context from prior literature on plant immunity, chitin perception, PRR signaling, RLCK function, stomatal immunity, and S-type anion channel regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C139, C146-C147, C151-C154, C156, C158-C159 accurately cite and represent extensive prior literature establishing the context for this work. These claims are appropriately referenced to published studies and provide the necessary background for understanding the significance of the current findings. They are not novel results but are correctly stated.
